title: Plan a 15-second product teaser from one approved still: keyframes, extensions, one edit and every delivery format
scenario: A candle brand wants a 15-second teaser, a stories version and a web header loop, all from one approved still. Your teammate wrote the plan and the budget. You review them before the first request. Use the exhibit. The brand, the files, the plan and the number of tries are made up for this case. The rates were copied from the Luma and Google pricing pages on 2026-10-07; they change, so check the live pages before you quote.
exhibit:
BRIEF (made up):
  Ember & Oak candle. One approved still: candle.png (16:9),
  the unlit candle on an oak table. candle-lit.png is an edit
  of the approved still with the wick lit.
  Deliver: a 15-second 16:9 teaser, a 9:16 stories version of
  the whole teaser, and a 5-second loop for the web header.

PLAN (draft, made up):
  Shot A   Luma ray-3.2, 5 s. The wick lights.
           video.keyframes:        [candle.png, candle-lit.png]
           video.keyframe_indexes: [0, 60, 120]
  Shot B   Veo 3.1 Lite, 8 s, 720p. The flame grows.
           Then extend Shot B once on Veo to reach the logo card.
  Cut      Join Shot A, Shot B and the extension in the editor,
           then cut the result to 15 s.
  Edit     Luma video_edit of Shot A: warmer evening light only.
           video.edit.strength: adhere_2
           aspect_ratio: 9:16 (to get a stories version of Shot A)
  Header   Luma ray-3.2, type video, 5s,
           video.start_frame candle-lit.png,
           video.end_frame   candle-lit.png, video.loop true
  Stories  Luma video_reframe of the whole 15-second teaser to 9:16
           at 1080p, in one request

BUDGET (rates from the pricing pages, 2026-10-07; tries made up):
  Shot A   Luma video, 720p, 5 s   $0.30 per 5 s x 3 tries      = $0.90
  Shot B   Veo 3.1 Lite, 720p      $0.05 per s x 8 s x 3 tries  = $1.20
  Edit     Luma video edit, 720p   $1.08 per 5 s x 2 tries      = $2.16
  Header   Luma video, 720p, 5 s   $0.30 per 5 s x 3 tries      = $0.90
  Stories  Luma reframe, 1080p     $0.36 per s x 15 s x 1 try   = $5.40
  Extension: not priced yet (the model may change).
  Luma reframe rates per second: 720p $0.12, 1080p $0.36

questions.prompt: Luma would refuse Shot A as written. Why?

options.text: The two lists have different lengths: two images, three frame numbers
options.explanation: Right. Luma says keyframes and keyframe_indexes must be the same length. Two images need two frame numbers.

options.text: Frame 120 is past the end, because a 5-second clip stops at frame 100
options.explanation: Luma's grid is seconds x 24, so a 5-second clip runs from 0 to 120. Frame 120 is in range.

options.text: Keyframes need a 10-second clip, so a 5-second clip cannot take them
options.explanation: Luma's multi-keyframe mode works at 5 or 10 seconds. Its own example pins three images on 5 seconds.

options.text: Frame 0 must be set with start_frame, so it can't be in the keyframes
options.explanation: A keyframe at 0 is the same as a start frame. Luma says to use one or the other, and the plan uses keyframes only.

questions.prompt: Shot B must be extended on Veo to reach the logo card. What is the problem?

options.text: Veo extends only 4k clips, so Shot B must be made at 4k first
options.explanation: It is the other way round: Google says Veo extension is limited to 720p videos.

options.text: Veo 3.1 Lite can't extend; make Shot B on Veo 3.1 or 3.1 Fast
options.explanation: Right. Google says extension is for Veo 3.1 and Veo 3.1 Fast models only, not Veo 3.1 Lite.

options.text: Veo extends a clip only if a voice is in its last second of video
options.explanation: That note is about carrying a voice across the seam (our reading). A silent clip can still be extended.

options.text: Veo can't extend at all, so extension is a feature of Luma only
options.explanation: Google documents extending Veo-made videos. Luma is not the only vendor that extends.

questions.prompt: The Edit sets aspect_ratio to 9:16 to get a stories version of Shot A. What will Luma return?

options.text: A 16:9 edit, because the setting is ignored; plan a reframe for 9:16
options.explanation: Right. Luma says the edit output keeps the source's aspect ratio, and aspect_ratio on an edit is silently ignored. A new shape is a reframe (chapter 6).

options.text: A 9:16 edit, so the Stories reframe line can come out of the plan
options.explanation: Luma keeps the source's shape on an edit. The 9:16 file still needs its own reframe.

options.text: No video, because Luma refuses any edit that sets an aspect_ratio
options.explanation: Luma does not refuse it. It ignores it silently, which is why it is easy to miss.

options.text: Both a 16:9 and a 9:16 edit, so the client can pick the better one
options.explanation: An edit returns one video in the source's shape. No second shape is made.

questions.prompt: Luma would refuse the Header request. Which change gives a valid seamless loop on Luma?

options.text: Remove loop, because the same first and last frame makes Luma loop
options.explanation: That is how you ask for a loop on Gemini Omni Flash. On Luma, loop: true is the setting for a seamless loop.

options.text: Remove end_frame, and keep start_frame and loop: true at 5 seconds
options.explanation: Right. Luma rejects loop with end_frame. A start frame, loop: true and 5 seconds is a valid loop from the still.

options.text: Move both images into keyframes at 0 and 120, and keep loop: true
options.explanation: Luma says keyframes is mutually exclusive with loop, so this is refused too.

options.text: Set the duration to 10s, so that the loop has more time to close
options.explanation: Luma rejects loop with 10s, and start and end frames with 10s too.

questions.prompt: The Stories line can't run as written. What should it become in the plan and the budget?

options.text: Two reframes at 720p (10 s + 5 s): 15 s x $0.12 = $1.80
options.explanation: Right. Luma's reframe source is capped at 10 seconds, so split the teaser. Vertical 1080p is not available yet, so use 720p.

options.text: Two reframes at 1080p (10 s + 5 s): 15 s x $0.36 = $5.40
options.explanation: The split is right, but Luma returns a coming soon 400 for 9:16 at 1080p.

options.text: One reframe at 1080p, since Luma splits it itself: $5.40
options.explanation: Luma says to split a longer clip into parts of 10 seconds or less yourself. And vertical 1080p is not available.

options.text: One 10 s reframe at 720p, drop the rest: 10 s x $0.12 = $1.20
options.explanation: The brief asks for a stories version of the whole teaser. Dropping 5 seconds misses the logo card.
